title: OurApp_vs_Obsidian
method: Manual expert inspection of retained real screenshots plus bounded source inspection; no new live device session

O01.state: Quick switcher with file paths and Find or create input

O03.state: Vault search, empty query; not search-result quality evidence

O06.state: Bold action on dedicated scratch note; keyboard visible

O11.state: Properties in note; metadata occupies substantial space

findings.title: The floating create action covers preview text
findings.task: Read the last visible note preview, then create a note.
findings.observed: In M01, New note sits over words in the orange note card. This is a visible obstruction, not just an aesthetic preference.
findings.comparison: O01 keeps file-choice rows and its search input distinct. It is a different retrieval surface, not proof that every Obsidian overlay avoids content.
findings.impact: The same small region must support reading and tapping; confidence in the card preview is reduced.
findings.direction: Keep the requested floating New note button. Reserve a readable safe area or adapt its placement; do not restore the rejected bottom create strip.
findings.acceptance: Recreate the three-card state, then test long titles, last-row scroll, list/grid, keyboard and large text. No required preview line or row action should be covered at rest.
findings.source: NotesController.renderHome: floating createRow; board bottom padding.
findings.limit: Not newly reproduced on a device. This does not prove the card is impossible to open or scroll.

findings.title: The search invitation is clipped
findings.task: Understand what the home search will search.
findings.observed: M01 shows the hint clipped after Search all content & s.... The full source hint is Search all content & settings.
findings.comparison: O01 uses Find or create a note; O03 presents a separate vault-search surface. Obsidian also has icon-learning costs.
findings.impact: The promise of a broad search is hidden exactly where a first-time user needs scope clarity.
findings.direction: Use a shorter visible invitation and an explicit scope explanation in the expanded search state, within the existing single bottom search.
findings.acceptance: At small width and large text, the primary search invitation remains understandable without guessing the clipped suffix.
findings.source: NotesController.renderHome: search.setHint and fixed filter control.
findings.limit: Clipping is visible; comprehension impact remains an expert judgment, not a user-study result.

findings.kind: Expert UX inference from visible UI
findings.title: Library mixes destinations with creation and intake
findings.task: Choose between browsing existing work, creating content and managing the app.
findings.observed: M02 mixes Archive, Trash, Voice inbox, Open file, Viewed files, + Checklist, Folders and Settings in one undivided list.
findings.comparison: O02 is a file-browsing surface; O04 separately exposes actions. This is a concept-boundary comparison, not equivalent menu inventories.
findings.impact: Users must infer which entries open places and which start operations. The app can feel like a collection of tools rather than one workspace.
findings.direction: Group the existing menu by purpose and make creation/intake roles consistent. Retain requested Folders/Settings ordering and do not add duplicate Notes/Doc entries.
findings.acceptance: Ask new users where to find a saved note versus create a checklist; record wrong turns before and after grouping.
findings.limit: No measured wrong-turn rate is available. Obsidian also distributes actions across several surfaces.

findings.title: Notes and Doc ask for an early classification decision
findings.task: Retrieve yesterday's content without remembering its creation mode.
findings.observed: M01 and M12 prominently separate Notes and Doc before showing content. Source implements independent workspace filtering.
findings.comparison: O01 presents several file kinds in one chooser. That does not mean MyNotes lacks cross-workspace search: its universal search already crosses Notes and Docs.
findings.impact: Mode recall can become an extra burden when users remember subject matter, not whether something was a Note or Doc.
findings.direction: Preserve both data models. Make retrieval scope and the current workspace obvious; use the existing global search as a reliable bridge rather than duplicating home controls.
findings.acceptance: Use mixed Notes/Docs with similar titles. Compare successful retrieval, workspace switches and backtracking, without instructing the creation mode.
findings.limit: Not a claim that tabs are intrinsically bad or that the two models must be merged.

findings.title: Folder browsing carries storage-management weight
findings.task: Open a folder during ordinary note organisation.
findings.observed: M03 repeats Folders / Your folders, explains private storage and originals, then includes Backups; source also appends Storage settings.
findings.comparison: O02 focuses on a collapsed fixture-folder tree. We did not execute a matched folder-navigation task in both apps.
findings.impact: Safety explanations are useful, but they compete with the everyday hierarchy and contribute to a settings-page feeling.
findings.direction: Keep accurate storage disclosures available, but progressively disclose management details away from the main folder list. Do not remove recovery routes.
findings.acceptance: With ten folders, the main task is immediately recognisable as browsing. Users can still locate backup and storage details without ambiguity.
findings.limit: The sparse fixture is not evidence that real users have no folders.

findings.title: Creating a folder adds a second sheet over Move to folder
findings.task: Create a destination while moving the current item.
findings.observed: M11 contains the dimmed editor, Move to folder and a second Create folder surface. Multiple dismiss/return levels are visible.
findings.comparison: No matched Obsidian create-while-moving capture is available. This is a directly observed MyNotes issue, not a claimed competitor speed win.
findings.impact: Users have to predict whether Create also moves the item, which layer closes, and where Back returns.
findings.direction: Use one clear staged flow inside the existing move surface, retaining the note and returning to the chosen destination. Keep the actual move outcome explicit.
findings.acceptance: Exercise Create, Cancel, system Back, invalid names and keyboard dismissal. Verify the correct destination and unchanged note contents after each branch.
findings.limit: No claim of data loss or broken Back behaviour is established by this image.

findings.title: Global queries silently change the filtering contract
findings.task: Search while a folder or label filter is active.
findings.observed: filterNow makes every nonempty query on page Notes global: folder, workspace and label filters are bypassed; nondeleted archived notes are included. This is deliberate code behaviour, not a measured bug.
findings.comparison: Obsidian separates quick switching, vault search and tags in O01/O03/O05. Their combined filtering semantics were not tested.
findings.impact: A user can think the query narrows the current list while the implementation broadens it. That undermines predictability.
findings.direction: Keep global search if intended. State All notes & Docs / includes archived explicitly and make switching to current-scope search understandable.
findings.acceptance: Populate two folders, two labels, Notes/Docs and an archive item. For each scope/query combination, verify the displayed scope and returned IDs against the stated contract.
findings.source: NotesController.filterNow: global; included; global || filter expression; renderUniversalResults.
findings.limit: Source establishes the branch. Its actual presentation with a populated global query needs fresh live capture.

findings.title: Universal results do not explain a body-text match
findings.task: Identify the right note when the search phrase is only in its body.
findings.observed: renderUniversalResults builds title buttons plus Note/Doc, archive and folder metadata. That renderer does not add a matching body passage or query highlight.
findings.comparison: O03 is an empty-query capture, so no claim about superior Obsidian snippets or search accuracy is made here.
findings.impact: Similar titles require opening candidates to discover why they matched; finding information is not the same as merely returning an item.
findings.direction: Add a compact, safe matching passage with highlighted terms and retain the already useful type/folder metadata. Preserve original text and bound long snippets.
findings.acceptance: Create five identically titled items with different body phrases. Identify the intended item from the result context, then verify the correct open target.
findings.source: NotesController.renderUniversalResults: title button and type/folder line.
findings.limit: M06 shows a focused search entry, not a matched global query. Source evidence supports this finding; comparative relevance is unmeasured.

findings.kind: Source-supported defect candidate; not live reproduced
findings.title: A filtered-empty library can look like a new empty library
findings.task: Understand why existing notes are not visible.
findings.observed: The emptyHint expression has a special no-labels-selected branch, but an ordinary nonempty label filter with zero matches and an empty query falls through to A little space for your ideas / Create a note below.
findings.comparison: O05 provides a tag-specific browsing context and counts. Its empty-tag state was not captured.
findings.impact: Users may create duplicate content or worry that saved notes disappeared when only the current view is empty.
findings.direction: Distinguish first-use empty, no results in this folder/filter, and loading/error states. Offer Clear filters without erasing actual content or preferences unexpectedly.
findings.acceptance: Keep a Work note, select a Personal-only filter, and clear the query. Confirm an accurate filtered-empty explanation and reversible clear action.
findings.limit: This follows a source branch. Reproduce on the signed build before assigning a confirmed runtime defect.

findings.title: A broad search is not yet a clear action-discovery route
findings.task: Find a less-frequent action without knowing its menu location.
findings.observed: Our Library and editor divide operations across menus and panels. Universal search source includes a small fixed set of settings destinations, not all editing actions.
findings.comparison: O04 visibly lists commands with a dedicated Select a command input. Execution of every action is not certified by that screenshot.
findings.impact: New users may know what they want to do but not the correct menu, especially after moving between Notes and Doc.
findings.direction: First improve grouping and wording. If testing still exposes discovery failures, add lightweight action help within existing navigation; do not copy a 205-command interface wholesale.
findings.acceptance: Give unprompted tasks such as change heading, move note and find within note. Record menu detours and help requests, not just eventual completion.
findings.source: NotesController.renderUniversalResults: fixed settings array; renderEditor menus.
findings.limit: No measured task-time advantage or missing-basic-search claim is made.

findings.title: Formatting plus keyboard squeezes out the writing context
findings.task: Format a phrase while retaining the surrounding paragraph.
findings.observed: M09 leaves only a short band of the note above the Format panel and keyboard. This directly shows how little prose remains visible in that captured state.
findings.comparison: O06 uses a compact toolbar above the keyboard while more of the note remains visible. Different fixtures prevent a precise productivity measurement.
findings.impact: Users may lose the sentence context, then need repeated panel closing and reopening to continue writing.
findings.direction: Adapt the existing single Format panel to available height; keep common controls compact and advanced options reachable. Preserve readable labels and the requested single A entry.
findings.acceptance: On the same device/font/IME, format the middle of a paragraph. Target at least three readable context lines at normal font, with a sensible large-text fallback and reachable caret.
findings.limit: The proposed context-line target is an acceptance proposal, not a measured current value for all devices.

findings.kind: Expert UX inference; existing accessible states acknowledged
findings.title: Selection versus future typing is not explicit enough visually
findings.task: Know whether Bold will affect selected words or the next typed words.
findings.observed: M17 and M18 show similar Format surfaces with different selection/caret states. Source has accessibility state descriptions, but the visible panel heading is simply Format.
findings.comparison: O06 shows an active selection near a compact toolbar. It does not establish that Obsidian solves every mixed-style state.
findings.impact: A styling operation can feel unpredictable even when the underlying span logic is correct.
findings.direction: Clarify the target inside the existing panel heading or concise context text. Preserve current selection, typing state, accessibility descriptions and Clear as the fifth inline action.
findings.acceptance: Alternate selected text, collapsed caret and mixed formatting. Users should predict the target before tapping and observe only the intended text change.
findings.limit: This is a comprehension risk, not a claim that formatting currently edits the wrong range.

findings.kind: Visible density plus source-confirmed panel contents
findings.title: Routine formatting shares space with advanced controls
findings.task: Apply a common style without navigating typography settings.
findings.observed: M10/M17 place paragraph choices, font family, Android size values and other options in a tall panel. FormatControls also provides Number paragraphs further down.
findings.comparison: O10 demonstrates configurable mobile toolbar actions. Customisation is not proof of a better default for novices.
findings.impact: More controls do not automatically make editing more effective; frequent actions compete with less-frequent configuration.
findings.direction: Prioritise frequent actions within the same panel and progressively disclose advanced options. Do not add another formatting strip or remove existing capabilities.
findings.acceptance: Observe five common formatting tasks and one advanced task. The common tasks should not require scanning advanced controls; the advanced task must remain discoverable.
findings.limit: Action frequency is not measured yet. Validate the prioritisation with actual users.

findings.title: Text-size controls expose implementation units
findings.task: Choose a comfortable reading/writing size.
findings.observed: M17 shows 18 sp. This is an Android implementation unit rather than a familiar task description for most note-taking users.
findings.comparison: O13 also exposes pixels in Appearance. Obsidian is not a plain-language ideal here; its font-size configuration is a different workflow, not numerical equivalence or a proved competitor advantage.
findings.impact: The control adds translation work for users who just want larger or smaller text.
findings.direction: Use understandable size wording and preview the effect while retaining precise accessible adjustment and the existing allowed range.
findings.acceptance: Ask users to enlarge text one step and restore it without explaining sp. Verify large-text layout, mixed selections and saved sizes remain correct.
findings.limit: Terminology judgment only; no unsupported contrast, physical-size or accessibility-failure claim.

findings.title: The persistent editor toolbar gives decoration equal weight
findings.task: Keep the main writing actions immediately understandable.
findings.observed: M07/M08 show Insert, Format, Voice and Background as equal persistent destinations. Background is always at the same hierarchy as writing operations.
findings.comparison: O10 allows toolbar configuration, but its icon density also increases learning effort. We should not imitate that density indiscriminately.
findings.impact: For a typing-centred workflow, attention may be spent on decoration while structural actions remain inside other menus.
findings.direction: Keep the useful labels and required actions. Test contextual prominence or configurable order inside the existing toolbar instead of simply adding more buttons.
findings.acceptance: Run typing, checklist and reorganisation tasks. Determine whether the toolbar order matches user intent before changing defaults.
findings.limit: Voice may be a primary workflow for some users. This is not an argument to remove or devalue it.

findings.kind: Candidate navigation gap in reviewed scope
findings.title: Long notes lack an established heading-jump counterpart
findings.task: Return to a named section in a long note.
findings.observed: M19 demonstrates a long scrollable note. No heading-outline surface was established in the reviewed MyNotes captures; source inspection did not establish a heading navigator.
findings.comparison: O09 visibly lists the note heading hierarchy in an Outline pane. Exact jump latency and every tap outcome were not measured.
findings.impact: Scrolling and text search are weak substitutes when users remember document structure rather than an exact phrase.
findings.direction: Evaluate a lightweight heading navigator that reuses existing heading formatting. Preserve scroll position and make return-to-edit straightforward; avoid introducing graph-style complexity.
findings.acceptance: Use a note with twenty headings and repeated words. Find a named section, edit it, and return to the previous location without losing selection or text.
findings.source: Reviewed NotesController and runtime Java navigation surfaces; no absence claim beyond this scope.
findings.limit: Potential missing interaction, not proof that all versions or hidden paths lack it.

findings.title: Mixed content looks like editable machinery even while reading
findings.task: Read prose and a checklist as one coherent note.
findings.observed: M13 exposes block borders, a block header, grip, pencil/menu controls and per-row controls between Before and After. The fixture name Checklist01 is test data, not proven default product copy.
findings.comparison: O07 integrates rendered headings, lists and callouts into note content. Obsidian metadata and its own toolbar still consume space.
findings.impact: Management chrome interrupts the reading hierarchy and can make a small amount of content feel more complicated than it is.
findings.direction: Offer calmer nonselected presentation and reveal object actions contextually without losing direct editing, grip behaviour, pen-scoped actions or accessibility.
findings.acceptance: Read a mixed note without editing, then edit one row and reorder one block. Compare comprehension and accidental edits while ensuring every existing action is still reachable.
findings.limit: This does not justify merging all object types or removing the existing safety controls.

findings.title: Several nearby menus require users to infer their scope
findings.task: Rename a block versus change or delete an individual list item.
findings.observed: M13 has a block-level pencil/overflow and multiple row overflows. The visual relationship between each action and its object must be learned.
findings.comparison: O08 illustrates integrated reading, not a verified equivalent list-management menu. No competitor interaction advantage is assumed.
findings.impact: Choosing the wrong scope risks unwanted structural changes and increases hesitation around editing.
findings.direction: Make selected-object boundaries and action wording explicit while retaining per-content actions, per-cell operations and confirmation before permanent deletion.
findings.acceptance: Ask users to change one row, rename its block and remove only that row. Record wrong-menu openings and verify unaffected content remains byte/semantically unchanged.
findings.source: NotesController content headers and item action menus.
findings.limit: Existing content descriptions are not assumed missing; TalkBack interaction was not tested in this review.

findings.title: Save/location confidence differs between note surfaces
findings.task: Leave the editor knowing where the work is and whether it is saved.
findings.observed: M07 has no visible saved-status text in its captured top bar. M14/M11 show a status string truncated to Saved · internal · D... or Saved · on this devi....
findings.comparison: Obsidian exposes a file/path context on several views, but we did not inspect a comparable failure/recovery indicator. It is not a proven save-reliability winner.
findings.impact: The user has to infer safety differently across surfaces; truncation removes meaning from already compact status text.
findings.direction: Define concise shared saving/saved/error feedback and a readable location detail on demand. Keep one compact top row; do not add permanent duplicate status bars.
findings.acceptance: Edit, wait for save, leave, reopen and inject a controlled write failure on disposable data. Status must match persisted content and keep recovery/Back safe.
findings.limit: No lost save or data corruption was reproduced. This is feedback design, not a persistence-failure assertion.

findings.title: Find-result context uses implementation-oriented wording
findings.task: Locate a phrase inside the current note and understand the hit.
findings.observed: M15 displays 1 match with Writing and a short passage; M16 correctly retains a highlighted hit after returning. The useful highlight should be preserved.
findings.comparison: A matched Obsidian in-note-find capture is unavailable in this evidence set. O03 is vault search and is not a valid substitute.
findings.impact: Writing is less precise than Body text or a user-facing content label in a mixed-content note.
findings.direction: Use concise content labels, accurate current/total hit feedback and consistent highlight visibility. Preserve the existing keyboard-aware field and successful highlighted return.
findings.acceptance: Search repeated text across body, checklist and table. Verify labels, next/previous order, close, keyboard placement and retention without changing content.
findings.limit: Do not relabel the existing highlighted return as broken; no comparative search speed was measured.
